name_en: Keichan — chicken and cabbage stir-fried in a house-blend sauce
summary_ja: 鶏肉とキャベツなどの野菜を、味噌や醤油ベースの特製だれで鉄板やジンギスカン鍋で焼く郡上市周辺の一品。卵を産まなくなった鶏を無駄なく食べたのが始まりと伝わり、味付けは店や家庭ごとに異なるという。
summary_en: Chicken and cabbage and other vegetables are seared on a griddle or Genghis Khan pan in a house-made miso- or soy-based sauce — a dish of the Gujo area said to have started as a way to use hens once they stopped laying, seasoning varying by household and shop.
source_title: 鶏ちゃん 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Funamiso — crucian carp slow-simmered with soybeans in red miso
summary_ja: 素焼きにした鮒を戻した大豆と時間をかけて煮て、豆味噌とざらめで仕上げる西濃地域の川魚料理。旨味の強い豆味噌が鮒特有の臭みを和らげるとされ、身がほろほろになるまで煮込んで冬の保存食とするという。
summary_en: Crucian carp, first grilled plain, simmers for hours with rehydrated soybeans, then finishes in soybean miso and coarse sugar — a river-fish dish of the Seino region, where the miso's strong umami is said to soften the fish's characteristic edge, simmered until the flesh falls apart as a winter keeping food.
source_title: 鮒味噌 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Otoshi no gottso — root vegetables simmered in a big pot for the year-end feast
summary_ja: 大根や人参、里芋などの根菜と糸昆布を一度に大鍋で煮て、大晦日から正月三が日にかけて温め直しながら食べる岐阜県の年越し料理。糸昆布には「細く長く生きられるように」との願いが込められているという。
summary_en: Root vegetables like daikon, carrot, and taro, along with shredded kelp, are simmered together in one big pot, then reheated and eaten from New Year's Eve through the first three days of the new year — a Gifu year-end dish where the kelp is said to carry a wish for a long, unbroken life.
source_title: 大歳のごっつぉ 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Imomochi — mashed rice and taro, grilled and dipped in ginger soy sauce
summary_ja: 里芋と米を一緒に炊いてよくつぶし、丸めて串に刺し炭火で焼いて生姜醤油をつける中津川市周辺の一品。稲刈り後のくず米と里芋を合わせたのが始まりとも伝わり、米が不作の年の「かさ増し」だったともいう。
summary_en: Taro and rice are cooked together, mashed smooth, shaped and skewered, then grilled over charcoal and dipped in ginger soy sauce — a dish of the Nakatsugawa area said to have begun with combining leftover broken rice from the harvest with sticky taro, or as a way to stretch rice in lean years.
source_title: いももち 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Akadatsu no subute — red taro-stalk strips dressed in a sweet vinegar
summary_ja: 里芋の赤紫色をした葉柄「赤だつ」の筋を取り、塩もみしてから合わせ酢で和える山県市の一品。石灰質のやせた土壌が芋の栽培に適した土地に伝わり、産後の体力回復を願って食べさせたとも言われている。
summary_en: The red-purple leaf stalk of taro, called akadatsu, has its fibers removed and is salt-rubbed before being dressed in a sweetened vinegar — a dish of Yamagata City on land whose lime-poor, thin soil suited taro cultivation, once said to be fed to new mothers to aid recovery.
source_title: 赤だつの酢ぶて 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kanboshi daikon ni — freeze-dried daikon simmered in dashi and soy sauce
summary_ja: 輪切りにした大根を茹でて串に刺し、氷点下の外気で凍結と乾燥を繰り返しながら1ヶ月ほどかけて飴色に仕上げる飛騨市山之村の特産品を、だし汁と醤油で煮る。標高850m超の「天空の里」で冬を越すための保存食という。
summary_en: Daikon, sliced into rounds, boiled, and skewered, is left in sub-zero air to freeze and thaw over and over across about a month until it turns amber — a specialty of Yamanomura in Hida City, over 850 meters up in what's called the 'sky village,' simmered here in dashi and soy sauce as a way to see out winter.
source_title: 寒干大根煮 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kuwanokimame ni — speckled heirloom beans simmered sweet in soy sauce
summary_ja: 赤いかすり模様の入ったさやごと乾燥保存できる「桑の木豆」を、柔らかくなるまで茹でてから醤油と砂糖で煮る山県市美山地域の一品。養蚕が盛んだった頃、桑の木の根元に植えて風から豆を守っていたのが名の由来と伝わる。
summary_en: Kuwanokimame, an heirloom bean speckled red and storable dried pod and all, is boiled tender before being simmered in soy sauce and sugar — a dish of the Miyama area of Yamagata City, named, it's said, for how the beans were planted at the base of mulberry trees to shelter them from wind during the region's silk-farming days.
source_title: 桑の木豆煮 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Komodofu — tofu boiled wrapped in a straw mat
summary_ja: 軽く水切りした豆腐をわら製のむしろ「こも」で巻いて1時間ほど茹で、無数の気泡とわらの香りをまとわせる飛騨地域の一品。だし汁で煮ても型崩れしにくく、正月や仏事のもてなし料理として親しまれてきたという。
summary_en: Lightly drained tofu is wrapped in a straw mat called komo and boiled for about an hour, taking on countless tiny air pockets and a hint of straw's scent — a dish of the Hida region that holds its shape well when simmered further in dashi, long served as a hospitality dish at New Year's and Buddhist rites.
source_title: こも豆腐 岐阜県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
